effect_estimate.comment: In Table 3, F-statistics are in parentheses next to p-values; in Table 4, B point estimates are in parentheses next to p-values with robust standard errors and 95% CIs. Group means in Section 4 text use European comma decimals in the original print (e.g., 52,0 and 57,0).
effect_estimate.value: In bootstrapped multivariate GLM regressions (N = 1,157 municipal-year observations, 2013-2020), intermunicipal consortium participation (Cooperation) had a statistically significant main effect on total log sanitation expenditure (F = 4.497, p = 0.034) and log sewage coverage (F = 4.938, p = 0.026), but not log water coverage (F = 0.468, p = 0.494). In parameter estimation with robust standard errors (Table 4), non-cooperating municipalities (Cooperation = 0 vs. Cooperation = 1) had significantly higher log sewage service coverage (B = 0.466, SE = 0.179, 95% CI [0.101, 0.815], p = 0.007; group means M = 57.0 vs. M = 52.0), non-significantly higher log water coverage (B = 0.064, SE = 0.056, 95% CI [-0.040, 0.177], p = 0.240), and marginally different log total expenditure (B = 0.404, SE = 0.232, 95% CI [-0.040, 0.858], p = 0.073; overall group means M = 6.1 for both groups). Transaction-cost proxies significantly predicted outcomes: contract management complexity (providing both water and wastewater vs. water only) increased log total expenditure (B = 0.095, SE = 0.044, 95% CI [0.012, 0.185], p = 0.024) and log sewage coverage (B = 0.075, SE = 0.032, 95% CI [0.012, 0.138], p = 0.014), with a significant Cooperation x Contract management interaction for total expenditure (F = 4.866, p = 0.028); log sewage investment increased log sewage coverage (B = 0.123, SE = 0.029, 95% CI [0.067, 0.181], p = 0.001) and log total expenditure (B = 0.109, SE = 0.029, 95% CI [0.049, 0.165], p = 0.002), with a significant Cooperation = 0 x sewage investment interaction on log sewage coverage (B = -0.081, SE = 0.034, 95% CI [-0.154, -0.017], p = 0.021) and log water coverage (B = -0.022, SE = 0.011, 95% CI [-0.043, 0.001], p = 0.049); and log water investment increased log water coverage (B = 0.025, SE = 0.011, 95% CI [0.008, 0.051], p = 0.016) while negatively associating with log sewage coverage (B = -0.070, SE = 0.027, 95% CI [-0.133, -0.030], p = 0.007).

mechanism_certainty.comment: Rated 1 (documented statistical association). Although framed as a panel comparison of cooperating versus non-cooperating municipalities, the study has Serious risk of bias due to baseline confounding and reverse causality (municipalities with low baseline sewage coverage self-select into consortia, as noted on p. 6) and relies on indirect secondary proxies for transaction costs (capital investment in R$ and single- vs. dual-service scope) rather than direct empirical observation of administrative/contractual mechanisms.
